If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over last 5 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to compensate for pessimism.  
In mid-horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment swings from positive to negative, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment drop.  
In late-horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment remains neutral (0.33–0.67), apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to align with historical mean reversion.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast exceeds 3σ above recent mean, reduce forecast by 2–3% in mid-horizon to prevent overfitting.  
If sentiment is negative but forecast is below 3σ below recent mean, increase forecast by 2–3% in mid-horizon to avoid underestimation.
